description.narrative:
The Youth Empowerment and Reintegration Project (YERP) is an initiative designed to address rural youth unemployment, reintegration of returnees and migration in Nigeria. YERP will empower 1,000 young Nigerians through climate-smart, sustainable agricultural opportunities, focusing on enhancing land ownership, agricultural training, and fostering a supportive market environment. The project's adoption of climate-resilient farming practices will promote environmental sustainability. YERP seeks to reduce irregular migration by providing viable local alternatives that offer long-term economic stability and resilience against climate-related challenges. Focused on Oyo State, the project emphasizes secure land tenure as a cornerstone of economic security for young farmers. By adopting sustainable land management practices and ensuring access to drought-resistant crops and water-saving technologies, YERP aims to reduce the environmental impact of agriculture, contribute to food security, and mitigate the effects of climate change. With a phased approach, YERP promotes community participation, stakeholder engagement, and ongoing monitoring to ensure adaptability and success. Collaboration with state government, private sector actors, environmental experts, and local communities is essential to developing a sustainable model for youth engagement in agriculture, ultimately contributing to both economic growth and the preservation of natural resources.
The proposed project focuses on the interconnections between youth unemployment, rural-to-urban movement, and irregular migration towards North Africa and Europe. It explores how land ownership and agricultural training can address these challenges by creating viable local livelihood options, reducing the need for risky migration.
